title: Principals and grants an engine exposes to the Security Manager tool
description: Declares only what no other descriptor holds: which kinds are principals, where they live, how the roster looks, and the shape of the grant model. Every kind, form field and option source is referenced by id and resolved against the engine's capabilities.json, forms/ and options.json by the validator; nothing is restated. An engine with no principals declares an empty list and a reason, and the tool is not offered (design Decision 5 and Decision 21).

reason.description: required when principals is empty: why the engine has no principals

status.description: complete: the descriptor-driven Security Manager serves this engine and its provider operations are round-tripped live; draft: declared but the engine stays on the previous manager until its operations are verified. Required when principals are declared.

access_notices.description: warnings the manager shows when the connected account could not read part of what it lists, so an empty or short roster is never mistaken for 'no principals'. Each reads a list of failures the provider reports on a resource of the given kind

kind.description: resource kind in capabilities.json whose family is 'role'; its form is the editor

label.description: singular name shown to the user (Role, User, Login)

scope.description: where the principal lives: server-wide or inside one database

identity.description: form field ids that together identify the principal, in display order (MySQL: name, host). Default: the kind form's name field

variant.description: selects the variant of a form shared by several kinds (Firebird, MySQL and MariaDB use one role form for user, role and grant)

columns.description: attributes of the listed resource shown as columns; the first is the principal's name

merged_into.description: kind of another principal whose roster lists this kind's resources too, for engines that keep one account catalog (MySQL accounts are users and roles alike). This kind then adds only a create action, and no roster or switcher entry of its own

field.description: native field of the listed resource

equals.description: the value that earns the marker

markers.description: labels shown beside a roster row when a native field of the resource has the given value; only facts the engine reports belong here

kind.description: principal kind a principal can be a member of

default_role.description: a membership can be marked as the member's default role

listing.description: where the listed resource carries its memberships and how to show them

native_field.description: key in the resource's native block holding one row per membership

equals.description: show Yes when the field equals this value, otherwise No

member_of_listing.description: where the selected principal carries the memberships it holds (the roles it belongs to), as opposed to listing, which is the principals that belong to it

native_field.description: key in the resource's native block holding one row per membership

equals.description: show Yes when the field equals this value, otherwise No

grant_kind.description: kind in capabilities.json that carries the grant and revoke operations

system_privileges.description: options.json dialect key listing the system or global privileges; absent when the engine has none as grants

object_privileges.description: options.json dialect key: a map from object kind to the privileges grantable on it

grantable_kinds.description: options.json dialect key: object kinds that can be granted on

column_privileges.description: object kind to the privileges that accept a column list; absent when the engine grants only on whole objects

grant_option.description: a grant can carry the option to grant it onward

granted_by.description: a grant can name a different grantor (Firebird GRANTED BY)

default_privileges.description: kind in capabilities.json holding default privileges, when the engine has them

listing.description: how to read the grants on one object from the provider's grant_kind resources: which native field names the object, grantee, privilege and so on, and what each stored privilege code means. Name the object with object_field, object_fields, kinds (per object kind, with a scope field) or embedded (grants carried on the object itself).

object_field.description: native field holding the granted object's name

grantee_kinds.description: stored grantee type code to the provider's grantee kind value

privilege_codes.description: stored privilege code to privilege name; a row whose code is not listed (memberships, DDL grants) is not an object grant. Omit when the engine stores privilege names directly

grant_option_equals.description: the stored value that means the grant carries the grant option

object_fields.description: native fields forming the object's path; the last is the object's name, earlier ones qualify it

scope_field.description: native field naming what a grant row is on (global, database, table, column, routine); used by kinds

kinds.description: object kind to how its grant rows are found, for engines whose grants are keyed by scope: the scopes it covers, the native fields forming its path (outermost first, matched against the tail of the object's path) and optional native values a row must have

grantee_template.description: how the selected principal is spelled in a grant row's grantee field, from native fields of the listed principal, in braces (MySQL: '{user}'@'{host}'). Default: the first identity field alone

held.description: show, for a selected principal, every grant it holds across all scopes (the only place global grants are visible)

held_across.description: an engine whose grants live inside each database (PostgreSQL ACLs on tables, functions): the held view also reads every connected database of this resource kind, at the target the prefix and the listed database's id field spell, and names the databases it could not read

kind.description: resource kind of a database in the server-scope listing

target_prefix.description: prefix of a database target id; the database's id field value follows it

id_field.description: dotted path in the listed database's native data that completes the target id

skip_field.description: dotted path in the listed database's native data that, when it equals skip_equals, marks a database that cannot be connected to (a template)

skip_equals.description: value of skip_field that skips the database

embedded.description: for engines that carry an object's grants on the object itself rather than as separate grant resources: the native field of the object's own listing entry holding one row per grant, optionally the same on child resources (column grants), and a native flag saying the rows are the object's default ACL because none is stored

default_flag.description: native boolean that is true when the rows are the family's default ACL, not stored grants

column.description: the child's display name is shown as the grant's column

status.description: Per feature status of the object-grants view: complete means the descriptor-driven view serves this engine's objects and its grant and revoke operations are round-tripped live; draft keeps the previous permissions matrix. Independent of the top-level status, which covers principals and membership. Required when grants are declared.

dialog.description: which fields of the grant and revoke operations the grants view fills in, so the shared view names no engine's field

object_type.description: field receiving the operation's own spelling of the object kind

qualifiers.description: fields receiving the path elements before the object's name (outermost first)

fixed.description: constant values the operation needs for object grants

object_arguments.description: an overloadable object (a function) is named by its argument types: the listed object's native field that holds them goes to the operation's field

row.description: how one listed grant prefills a revoke

grantee_field.description: field receiving the grantee as a name

grantee_grid.description: a grid of one value per grantee (PostgreSQL: a role) or of separate user and host values (MySQL); the listed grantee is split into them when a host is declared

privilege_key.description: when privileges is a grid, the column holding the privilege name; otherwise rows are plain names

columns_key.description: grid column receiving a column list; present when the engine's revoke accepts a column list for a column grant row

object_by_kind.description: object kind to the field that receives its name instead of object (MySQL: a database's name goes to its database field)

object_type_by_kind.description: object kind to the operation's object type value when the kind's own name is not one (PostgreSQL grants on a view with TABLE)

qualifiers_by_kind.description: object kind to the qualifier fields that apply to it, replacing qualifiers (PostgreSQL: a schema or database is not qualified by a schema)

kind.description: resource kind carrying the failure list (server)

native_field.description: dotted path in that resource's native block to an array of failure rows

match.description: native field of a failure row to the value, or list of values, that makes the notice apply; every entry must match
